summary: Evidence-based audit of authentication-cookie configuration (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Domain scope, lifetime, and __Host-/__Secure- prefixes) for applications you are authorized to test. Returns PASS, FAIL, or INCOMPLETE with rule IDs and fixes, and never returns cookie values.
useWhen: Adding a session-cookie check to a login test, AI browser-agent workflow, or CI pipeline for your own application.
Verifying that a Browser Use or Playwright login creates an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite-restricted session cookie.
Giving an MCP client a bounded, policy-fixed way to audit Set-Cookie headers on configured origins.
doNotUseWhen: Testing websites you do not own or are not authorized to test.
Proving exploitability, XSS, CSRF, or server-side session security; CookieGuard audits configuration only.
Reading, exporting, or replaying cookie values or browser profiles.

tested: Linux (CI) and macOS arm64 (local), Node.js 24, Chromium

integrations.install: npx --yes cookieguard-ci@0.2.0 scan http://127.0.0.1:3000/ --auth-cookie session_id --format json

requires: GitHub-hosted or self-hosted runner with Node.js 24 setup
A startup JSON configuration with allowedOrigins
tested: Official MCP SDK client on Linux (Node.js 24) and macOS (Node.js 26)

integrations.install: Copy skills/cookieguard-browser-auth-security into your agent skills directory, or add the repository as a Claude Code plugin marketplace.
requires: An agent that supports Agent Skills (SKILL.md)

operations.description: Audit cookies created while your own test code drives an authorized browser workflow, such as a login.
permissions: Your test code owns the browser session; the collector starts before the workflow and observes only allowed origins
operations.network: None beyond the workflow the browser already performs.

operations.description: Send one GET request (plus same-origin redirects) and audit the Set-Cookie headers.
inputs: URL on loopback or an explicitly allowed origin, without credentials, query, or fragment
permissions: Loopback by default; nonlocal origins need --allow-origin; the MCP server needs an exact startup allowlist
operations.network: GET without cookies or authorization headers; bodies are discarded.

operations.description: Re-evaluate a sanitized CookieGuard JSON report or Browser Use result under the current policy.
inputs: MCP cookieguard_audit {"evidenceFile": "name.json"} inside the configured evidenceDir
permissions: Local file read only; the MCP server reads only plain .json names inside its startup evidenceDir

operations.description: Optional read-only cookieguard_audit action an agent can call mid-run. Provisional; it cannot satisfy policy.
permissions: Registered by developer code with audit.register_tools(tools)

operations.description: Explain a rule ID, incomplete reason, error code, or status without any cookie data.

checks.title: Missing HttpOnly
checks.confirmedWhen: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed without HttpOnly.
checks.reviewWhen: A cookie that only heuristics suggest is authentication-related lacks HttpOnly.
checks.fix: Set HttpOnly on the authentication cookie at the server.

checks.title: Missing Secure
checks.confirmedWhen: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed without Secure.
checks.reviewWhen: A cookie that only heuristics suggest is authentication-related lacks Secure.
checks.fix: Set Secure and serve the application over HTTPS.

checks.title: SameSite declaration violates policy
checks.confirmedWhen: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed with a declared SameSite value outside allowedSameSite, or with no declaration while requireExplicitSameSite is set.
checks.reviewWhen: The same condition on a cookie whose authentication role is unconfirmed.
checks.fix: Use an allowed SameSite value, or explicitly adjust the policy for a reviewed cross-site flow with separate CSRF defenses.

checks.title: Domain sharing requires review
checks.confirmedWhen: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed with a Domain attribute while requireHostOnly is set.
checks.reviewWhen: A Domain attribute without requireHostOnly, or on a cookie whose role is unconfirmed.
checks.fix: Omit Domain when subdomain sharing is unnecessary; use a valid __Host- cookie where practical.

checks.title: Authentication-cookie lifetime exceeds policy
checks.confirmedWhen: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed with a remaining lifetime above maxLifetimeDays.
checks.reviewWhen: The same condition on a cookie whose authentication role is unconfirmed.
checks.fix: Reduce Max-Age or Expires to the configured maximum and enforce server-side session expiry.

checks.title: Invalid security prefix declaration
checks.confirmedWhen: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed in a Set-Cookie header that violates its prefix requirements.
checks.reviewWhen: The same header violation on a cookie whose authentication role is unconfirmed.
checks.fix: Use HTTPS and Secure for both prefixes; __Host- also requires an explicit Path=/ and no Domain.

checks.title: Authentication-cookie protection regressed
checks.confirmedWhen: A comparable baseline shows that a confirmed authentication cookie lost Secure, HttpOnly, host-only scope, a Lax/Strict SameSite declaration, or its lifetime limit.
checks.reviewWhen: Never; incomparable baselines produce no CG007 findings.
checks.fix: Restore the previous protection or review and document the intentional policy change.

checks.title: Authentication role is unconfirmed
checks.confirmedWhen: Never; this is always a review item.
checks.reviewWhen: A cookie looks like authentication to the uncalibrated classifier, or its role is unknown, and it was not configured.
checks.fix: Identify the actual session cookie in your login test and configure its exact name or validated scoped evidence.

checks.title: Cookie evidence requires review
checks.confirmedWhen: Never; this is always a review item.
checks.reviewWhen: Attributes, the SameSite declaration, or browser acceptance are unknown or ambiguous.
checks.fix: Start collection before login and inspect the server cookie configuration. Do not infer declarations from browser defaults.

statuses.label: PASS
statuses.meaning: The audit completed with no confirmed violations at or above failOn. It covers only the configured checks and does not prove application security.

statuses.label: FAIL
statuses.meaning: Confirmed authentication-cookie policy violations at or above failOn were observed.

statuses.label: INCOMPLETE
statuses.meaning: Evidence was missing or the audit could not complete. Never a pass.

findingStatuses.meaning: Observed violation on a cookie whose authentication role was confirmed by developer configuration or validated evidence. Can fail a run.
Heuristic or uncertain finding (classifier-only identity, unknown attributes, or ambiguous evidence). Never fails a run.

evidenceSources.meaning: Parsed from an observed Set-Cookie header.
Read from browser cookie-store metadata; cannot show the original SameSite declaration.
Supplied cookie metadata, such as a JSON cookie array.
Imported from a legacy extension result.

privacy: Cookie values are never written to results, reports, logs, or MCP responses.
No telemetry, accounts, or remote services. The engine runs locally.
HTTP scans send no cookies or authorization headers and discard response bodies.
CookieGuard never asks for, stores, or replays credentials or session tokens.
MCP responses withhold observed cookie names, domains, and paths unless a name is a configured authentication cookie.
authorization: Audit only applications you own or are authorized to test.
Loopback targets by default; every nonlocal origin must be explicitly allowed. Private non-loopback addresses and remote IPv6 are rejected in HTTP scans.
The MCP server fixes its allowed origins, policy, and evidence directory at startup; tool arguments cannot change them.
evidenceRequirements: Configure the exact authentication-cookie names. Without them, findings stay in review and authentication rules cannot fail a run.
Start browser collection before the login and evaluate after the workflow completes.
Audit the response or workflow that actually sets the session cookie; otherwise the result is INCOMPLETE.
SameSite declarations need Set-Cookie header evidence; browser-store evidence leaves them unknown.
limitations: Configuration audit only: no exploit, XSS, CSRF, or server-side session validation.
A PASS covers only the configured checks and observed cookies.
HTTP header scans cannot log in or execute JavaScript.
Browser verification is Chromium-family only; Windows and Browser Use cloud browsers are untested.
Classifier outputs are uncalibrated triage and never confirm authentication identity.
Exposing a tool cannot force an agent to call it; enforce results in tests or CI.
